result.summary: Adds configuration and parameters for Testnet 5 (BIP 95), including chain parameters, DNS and fixed seeds, kernel C API support, and GUI/CLI integration. Testnet 5 eliminates the 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception from earlier testnets, sets a higher minimum difficulty (nBits 0x1a0fffff), and enforces BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) rules from block 1. Only the top seven commits belong to this PR, with the preceding commits implementing BIP 54 via stacked PR #35793.
result.problem: Testnet 3 and Testnet 4 frequently suffer from block storms and severe difficulty manipulation due to the 20-minute minimum-difficulty rule, disrupting developers and testers. Additionally, there is currently no public test network validating BIP 54 consensus cleanup rules from genesis.
evidence: PR description: 'Relative to Testnet 4 it removes the 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception, raises the minimum difficulty, and enforces BIP 54 from block 1.'
PR description references IRC discussion agreeing to settle Testnet 5 changes alongside BIP 54 before shipping in a release.
result.scope_notes: This PR is stacked on top of PR #35793 (BIP 54 implementation). Only the top seven commits belong to this PR; the remaining 22 commits represent the unmerged BIP 54 stack. The genesis block has not yet been mined.
result.changed_since_previous: Added DNS seeds and fixed seeds for Testnet 5, added BIP 95 to doc/bips.md, and added release notes.
result.card: Adds Testnet 5 (BIP 95) parameters, seed nodes, kernel bindings, and command-line options to Bitcoin Core. Testnet 5 eliminates the 20-minute minimum-difficulty rule that caused block storms on Testnet 3 and Testnet 4, raises the minimum difficulty, and enforces BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) rules starting from block 1. The pull request is stacked on top of unmerged prerequisite PR #35793 (BIP 54), with only the top seven commits specific to Testnet 5. The genesis block has not yet been mined.

risk.why: Touches chain consensus parameters and includes BIP 54 validation enforcement in the stacked commits; flaws could cause chain splits or consensus divergences on the new network.
